posts.title: Destiny.
posts.author: Peter White
content: The sun falls from its thrown
And we’ll have to head home
But I know you’re wrong,
About destiny.
All stars have their path,
And clouds block them too.
You go your own way,
And I’ll turn my back.
The tides rise in vain,
As the beach still endures.
Our shackles are strong,
And the road will be steep.
But I hope you’re wrong,
About destiny.

posts.title: In Search of the Answer.
posts.author: Peter White
content: Like the moon seen in the morning.
Like love found without knowing.
It appears without warning.
Behind the celestial dome, maturing.
Or under the surface, obscuring.
Now, and always alluring.
I will check under the streetlights, strolling.
You can search in our minds, dreaming.
Still for now, just waiting.

posts.title: In the End
posts.author: Peter White
content: Steps will follow steps, each in their turn;
The world moves and changes shade.
Slow to fast and light to dark,
All things arriving at the urn.
Bathe in the beauty today,
The maple and the lark.
For when spring turns to summer,
And June follows the flowers in May,
The snow will follow too, never delayed;
Then the cycle slows, things different than they were.

posts.title: Or In the Wildflowers.
posts.author: Peter White
content: Through a meadow, in the mountains,
On the train, plane, or nowhere at all!
Anywhere at all, anytime, and any-why.
It will always happen; cannot be stopped.
It’s okay to smile, shout, cry, and dance.
The food fight builds courage.
The skinny dip finds a youthful heart.
Pay no mind at all, to who said different.
They cannot, or do not, see
The forest through the trees.

posts.title: Not Supposed to be Free.
posts.author: Peter White
content: I guess we're not supposed to be free
if all those who love, will someday be grieved.
All in shackles pass too, though with much less adieu,
but I guess we're not supposed to be free.
Consider the wren, but more, consider his plight.
Think of the train, who does just what is right.
Now turn to within where choice breeds despair.
What to eat? And where to go? Chop my hair,
but who should care? It only gets deeper.
The choice to leave, you say, "What's the matter?"
They want to be free, but that will hurt you.
so let go of your choice, be un-free too.
I guess we're not supposed to be free
maybe love is a curse we no longer need.
Your life isn't easy, so we can make it a breeze,
cuz I guess we're not supposed to be free.
Move aside for the plan, and a good life.
No more mistakes; at least none by your knife.
Of course  this is right, there's no other way.
Your pleas are not the law, that's why they won't stay.
You're telling them now, "It's bigger than you."
And yes, you do mean it. Let's tame the shrew
whose goal must be selfish. Think of the wren,
safe in his cage, and still free to no end!
I guess we're not supposed to be free,
for how can they know what sacrifice to make?
No one knows best, and especially not you,
but I guess we're not supposed to be free.

posts.title: Antiques and Collectables.
posts.author: Peter White
content: The old antique shop shut down,
and I will love you forever.
That's just business, they say.
If no one is buying, you
aren't really selling. This town
won't support you, so
it's time to move on.
Where you stood is still empty,
because I will love you forever.
Memories don't sell like they used to,
so we let the dead things die.
dust won't forget, so don't sweep
and let it mourn. Your blinds are
still drawn, so it's time to move on.
A Goodwill opened uptown,
and it's new and it's different,
but parts feel the same. There's no
dust yet, and I found a nice dresser,
and, actually, another one too.
There's rows of benches and baths, but
I can't find any dust yet. There's paintings,
or prints? a desk, and fine china, but
I can't find any dust yet. Shopping carts glide
on polished linoleum, as I float by
an empty lot on the way home.
A new table in hand, I try
to move on. It sits in the corner,
but I still can't find any dust yet.
I don't go uptown anymore,
so I can love you forever.

posts.title: Yellow Birch Succession.
posts.author: Peter White
content: There is art in being here.
Take unconditional breath
and let the moss spread.
There is genius in this place.
For thought will come, yet,
somehow, it will ask for nothing.

posts.title: Shoelace Express.
posts.author: Peter White
content: The street was black beneath
my feet, which continued their walkin'.
The street turned black and
my feet continued their walkin'.
My feet turned back, so
I had to look up.
To look up and see, a bird
on the ground, just one
star in the sky, and the
dog's on the roof. On the
roof, I look up. I look up to see,
There's a sky in the puddle
and my feet staring back at me.

posts.title: There's a Bucket in That Tree.
posts.author: Peter White
content: The summer ends in rain.
Sweaters employed to shield
this first of cold skies,
who warns fairly of what's to come.
The fall passes by, under rain.
After the sky turned cold,
the sweet gum tried again
to sow its seeds, into better times.
The spring comes, of course, with rain.
the winter sky struggles to wake,
while daffodils pierce a white veil.
The rain falls, still, and turns
the wheel. One thousand years
to bury the sweet gum's burr.

posts.title: On Peace.
posts.author: Peter White
content: The pressure relieves & subsides
not just among
the plants & the trees,
but wherever I am Free.

posts.title: A Moment Before the Next.
posts.author: Peter White
content: Fleeting, fluttering for a
moment or two- or for them
it was forever. By my
count it was a summer
of days cut short and
thoughts unsaid. Even so
it was a season of love-
of longing for such a fleeting
fulfillment. A summer sun filled
so briefly like the breath
that holds petunias. Just for
a moment; to them: forever.

posts.title: Mourning for Light
posts.author: Peter White
content: The wind bites down and clamps its maw,
And in its wake the meadow calms.
Black as souls that no love has known,
The sky shows fauns that are not there,
And I hear songs from winter birds.
Cold iron lays limp in my lantern,
And freezes the world where it lays.
One day, and it will have been soon,
The sun will come, and I will mourn at
greater intervals, pray to him in days between.

posts.title: The Jolly Roger
posts.author: Peter White
content: The sheets are filled with the wind that
carries your scented lotion
and on the hill recoils, cracks, and creaks
against the waves which are
what could go wrong.
Still this voyage drags along
the coast which nags, reminds me of home.

posts.title: The Lonesome
posts.author: Peter White
content: A branch fell into the woods-
and the woods would soon follow.
Taking the thrush, the beetles,
the berries the same, into the lonesome.
After the fall, the woods must
celebrate. A feast from us, and for
our long lonesome. The woods feast
completely, and sacrifice fully.
We risk winter for the spring,
and remember the fallen.
The lonesome, though long, cannot be forever
For the woods tend towards us, as long as we follow.

posts.title: A Warm Yellow Light.
posts.author: Peter White
content: I want to paint my soul orange
and fill my heart with the sun.
I want the Earth to thank me
for the thanks I give it.
I want to feel the sun set
and sleep with my mind quiet.
I need to become a warm
yellow light. On a thunderstorm night.
When the sun sets to early.
and I need to become a warm yellow light.

posts.title: Native Hill (A Heron's Goodbye.)
posts.author: Peter White
content: When the trillium begins to bloom
and the streams cannot be ephemeral.
Then she will wake in the mountains
and drink from the maple.
Drink deeply, and follow the streams-
quick, before the laurel can wilt.
She'll dance in summer flowers
while her feet become planted.
Strawberries ripen and the roots rise.
The vine of the sweet pea caresses her calf,
guiding her gently and into the valley.
Still, vines will creep higher, and their leaves
will soon fall; lay in her colors as
she turns to the sky.
her hair will be feathered with
the heron's goodbye-

posts.title: To-Do List
posts.author: Peter White
content: There are one thousand things to do;
and I'll start by laying here.

posts.title: How to Write a Poem
posts.author: Peter White
content: On a saturday morning, nothing
has to be perfect. The end
of the week is for poetry.
Time for one's self, no one else.

posts.title: The Red Oak
posts.author: Peter White
content: Seasons are delayed between
city buildings. The Red Oak waits
to provide an encore seen by few.
The Sycamore's leaves have
long since been taken, now
the ground may be painted like
a sunset. If she waits long enough
the early snow may preserve her
work. Things don't work like
they used to, and the seasons find
pause in the alley. Just peaking
above my bedroom window,
The Red Oak missed the signs
from her friends, but hurried
when she could, just a moment
late, applauded for her untimely show.

posts.title: Revisiting.
posts.author: Peter White
content: I ran my fingers through
your hair and your memories.
There was knot after knot
like fresh fallen boulders.
Content in their space,
the comb simply had to give way.
At the end of this strand,
my hand was released
now heavy and dark, unwilling
or unable to brush you again.

posts.title: To visit old Friends.
posts.author: Peter White
content: To visit old friend,
one has to call first.
To call old friends
first, one must be accepting.
To grow bigger than one's past
old friends must be forgiven.
But, "old friends," one thinks,
"are old friends for a reason."
To visit old friends,
one must wait for them to call first.
An old friend, if they were,
must surely call on one's birthday.
and if they do not, for many years running,
one must wait another.
for old friends were friends once,
and once can't help remembering.

posts.title: The River's Always Flowing
posts.author: Peter White
content: I live on the river's bank
with the beaver and the bear.
The beaver dams a tributary
and feels secure, though I am wary
It's all held back for the moment,
but the pressure builds, until the torrent.
I go swimming when the weather's right
like before the rains or a summer night.
I swim contented in the river's flow
but tire quickly with no dam to slow it.
I lived by the river once
like the beaver, but not the bear.
The bear, I witnessed, held his ground
patiently waiting all seasons 'round.
He did not give way like me,
or the beaver. He stood, so serenely,
and I know he sees clearly.

posts.title: To find a Silent Step.
posts.author: Peter White
content: I look to you in the days that drift, Dance, and die.
In those times, I stop my wonder.
I stop my wonder
to find one silent step,
but seldom succeed. I search,
and find myself wandering,
wondering: How would a shoelace think?
Instead of will, they live by drift,
always dancing life into ever flowing life.
But really they step how I step
and dance only when I tell them.
And me? Well, I only dance on drifting days.
On days when steps fall silent
on  a welcoming soft ground.
I only dance when you tell me.
I only drift to stop the wonder.
I only stop when I wonder,
"Where can I take one silent step?"
Before my eyes fall down.

posts.title: Cicada Concerto
posts.author: Peter White
content: It becomes possible to think of going
only after the weather changes.
When the clouds come down
from on high, and force all to bask
in them. When rain wets your bones,
Pleading, Begging you to go home.
Even when the sun is out,
just think of going.
When the song birds wait while
the cicadas sing, or the wind
blows loud. Smell spring ground
and listen to traffic. Only then
can you think of going.

posts.title: Thank You
posts.author: Peter White
content: I am a very boring and unpleasant
man, stuck here, where I stand.
My thoughts, they lay still,
though I feel them rush over me.
Like the landslides that steals the tree
from his place in the valley.
'Thank you,' I whisper, and I promise
I mean it. But I had an orange with lunch today
and can think only that I should have shared it.
It was delicious and vibrant, full and complete,
just a few wedges too many.
Though I could never figure out how
to give them to you.
'Thank you,' I say, this time so it may be heard.
Though I only wish I had meant it.
I feel I am a boring and unpleasant kind of man,
though I know no other way of being.
I ate an orange with lunch today,
and the truth is I only thought now
of sharing it.

posts.title: Puhpowee
posts.author: Peter White
content: Thoughts I can't think are wrought
by word I don't mean.
Rocks who lay covered by beds
stir motion in their bay,
and ships pass in an eternal
night, as the lips of two
lovers cursed to fight
lives in long parted places.
Only a fool would fight currents, but I think I could.

posts.title: A Lumberjack
posts.author: Peter White
content: One day the executioner will shed his cloak
and reveal that he
is me.
On that day, I will smile,
and he should smile back.
As he swings his ax,
and we both know he must,
I will be a chestnut tree.
With each blow
I will recount the years. And
through the years,
in every moment,
between every swing,
I will see the same hooded figure.
Not guiding me, not hiding
only waiting.
As the tree falls,
and the final blow lands,
our smiles become cemented.
A chestnut falls, and none should weep.
A chestnut falls, and its smile lives on.
100 years and the chestnut rises again,
waiting, again,
for the executioner to lift his hood.

posts.title: Transcendence
posts.author: Peter White
content: The sky glowed inside me,
and finally I felt it.
Of course I love you!
Finally I felt it.
Finally, warm enough.
Enough to tell you, 'I love you.'
And how could I not?
The sky glowed inside me,
I swear it.
I could hear the sunset and
feel the flock that flies South.
And finally, I saw you feel the same things.
Of course I love you!
It's nice to meet you, here.
Yes, (that's right) I love you, too!

posts.title: Terrible Master (The End of the Tour)
posts.author: Peter White
content: The mind makes promises
But soon forgets;
Between the incessant nature of our body,
And the roar of the wind,
And the hat that’s getting itchy,
And our friend that
Isn’t anymore,
The buzz in our pocket,
And the song that must be skipped,
Or also the decision that now is the time
To start heading home because maybe
We didn’t make enough time for ourselves today.
The mind makes promises,
And tries so hard;
Like lumber trying to see the forest;
But is doomed to forget.
Start, we must think,
By removing the hat,
Maybe throw it in with the laundry.
Then, forgive the hands for being hands,
And the mind for the thoughts we think.
Spit out the blood.
Or at least as much as we can think to.
And please, we remind ourselves,
Forgive the hands for the way they are.
The mind will keep making promises,
Bless our heart,
But please keep in mind,
It is our nature to forget.

posts.title: Orange Juice
posts.author: Peter White
content: Another sun rises and I try
to make a plan. There's work
to be done, so I start by
drawing the curtains. The pinkish
red blinds me for a second.
"I have time,"
I think.
So I lay back in bed. Children
want to be superheroes and adults
have late nights (or is it early mornings?)
when they try to remember why.
Before an answer is found, life's
duties get in the way.
"I have to get groceries,"
I think.
So I grab a new note and survey
my kingdom. No milk, no eggs.
I should have salad more than--
Okay, I should get a salad.
Another few minutes passed by
my head in the open fridge,
and finally the note approximates
what an adult should eat.
"It's probably busy right now,"
On a Thursday at 10.
I pick up a book, I think
of the first time I read it,
how inspired I felt to--
my other hand commands
my attention, and now its 11.
"I have to get groceries,"
A thumb still marks my page.
So I pull it away, and walk out
the door. A dull grey sky is easier
on the eyes, and I remember wanting
to fly as a kid. Would make this walk
a bit more bearable.
In the aisles, I'm alone, but my music
is a bit too loud, and I look around
expecting to find someone I've bothered.
"Eggs, check. Milk, check."
I say in my mind.
"Bread, cereal, frozen lasagna,"
"flour, sugar,"
I pass by the salads.
Kids have it easy. Chicken nuggets when
you can't stomach asparagus. Mothers
to kiss you better-- salad as an ultimatum!
There's something I'm forgetting...
"Yogurt,"
I skip the song that's just too long.

posts.title: June, Again
posts.author: Peter White
content: You know where I'll be,
and I hope to see you then.
For when the fig should fall,
there is orchard begging me.
And when I chase her call
a serpent is all I see.
Tell me he's in your heart too,
and I will listen to no end.
But, the space inside time as it passes
harbors the truth that neither may share.
Like a priest who pacifies masses,
Our gods ought not be laid bare.
Let summer come, as it may,
and only on the solstice know that it is June, again.

posts.title: The Dust in my Palms.
posts.author: Peter White
content: And I carried that flame,
until its heat became my own.
And I don't visit that tomb,
yet your ashes are still in my hand.

posts.title: The Sun Sets Last on the Old Oak Tree.
posts.author: Peter White
content: Oh, to steal the final light, from boughs on high, to join that sweetest Earth’s choir of angels. That final light, with warmth so kind, begs to all, "Return! Return! Abandon your winter roosts! Follow now, to Northern Skies!" And of course, I listen, for Spring’s warmth knows not a lie. Still, I ask, take me for no fool, only the wary may outlast those days that winter hides. Those days when the sun still sets early, and feeds on the young and old finding themselves enchanted by prospects of prosperity. Those days of cruel deception.

No, I speak now of a day’s long warmth, which promises itself tomorrow. I speak of the sun who ambles on through blue painted canvas. I speak of that sun with the strength to shine through the intrusion of clouds. I sing now, for I have arrived again to be the evening’s choir. True, though it is, that the days still must end; the nights are not quite as long. All those I sing to remember the cold, and so hold dearly to the light. Oh, the touch of that bronze glow, come now and hear us. Oh, the life that may continue to live, come now and see us. Take these notes that we sing—oh, that song that is sung to the angels themselves—take these notes and I hope, how sincerely I hope, you may join us in this final light.

posts.title: Specifically, For You.
posts.author: Peter White
content: I.
And we stood, together in the warm embrace of flame.
In the morning, dew would set,
mournful doves would coo;
And in those dark blue woods,
you would turn your back, and I would too.
II.
Lost in small thoughts, between moments,
smaller still, I look up and notice now.
Your gait is not the same as before.
The space continues to grow,
the path bends into undergrowth
and I get lost in small thoughts,
between moments,
smaller still.
III.
Nothing is like it was before,
nothing ever was. Today I search
for us, but find blackened leaves,
trodden on, through a worn path.
I don't want to be fated.
I want to choose. I search the space
between leaves, and remember the Spring.
That is enough.

posts.title: Sonnet 1
posts.author: Peter White
content: When songs are sung into eternity.
When names are hewn beyond the touch of time.
We write ourselves into antiquity,
In rooms we lay, the moss will cloud our names.
The skin retreats, and even bones abide.
Till fungus feasts on all that I became.
I weep no tears, and in the dirt confide.
When joy is shared and moments may pass by.
When life is lived, in spite of death's approach.
The glass will break; branches bend to untie.
Ours is now, while the end will still encroach.
Lord time, do your worst, and I will stay here.
Tomorrow fades premature, now is clear.

posts.title: Elegy for Dandelions
posts.author: Peter White
content: For decades now, she has lain.
Inside my shadow, beyond my gaze.
Where once she danced, now nothing grows,
but coral bells, and blades of grass.
Each Spring I try, with shows of blooms,
to call her back, to fill my glade.
Though blue birds fly and the moon does wane
her star won't shine till I am gone, and born again.
Her yellow petals strewn about,
in times when I dared grow taller.
I still recall that wordless banter,
and only now I strain to shout.
I shout and scream but leaves still grow.
Wind still blows, and snow still falls.
That cursed sun still burns brighter.
I shout, I try, at least, but branches reach.
And with their reach my love is buried deeper.
The meadows retreat, and mocking birds whimper.
I dream of days decades ago.
I dream of a life that once was simpler.

posts.title: What Came of Picking Flowers. (sonnet 2)
posts.author: Peter White
content: I waited for Spring, and now wish that I hadn't.
Had it still been the fall, this might not have happened.
But snow did stop falling, and song birds formed choirs,
and flowers did bloom, but why did I pick them!
I love them so dearly
in their vase by my bed.
But all things decay,
and soon will be dead.
I waited for Spring, and her yellow petals
make me wish that I hadn't.

posts.title: Untold.
posts.author: Peter White
content: Ridges may tell no lie,
nor the rain that befalls them,
so artists try to do the same.

posts.title: I think I'm an Earth sign?
posts.author: Peter White
content: The Mind Travels to Odd Places When You Don't Think of Letting it. / Now & Therefore Forever.
There can't be a number
to describe how I live.
Not how many times I have loved, or will love.
Nor how many days that I will see.
The market decides,
and the data tells all,
but it can't tell me.
You could count how many
times I've seen or will see
that pink Dogwood tree.
But don't tell me, because
there is nothing it could mean
that I don't already know.
What I know is that I see it now
and therefore forever.

posts.title: At Eternity's Gate
posts.author: Peter White
content: Poorer now, for having lost touch with eternity.
Poorer still, for waking now in this new world.
One which has lost this feeling;
but kept the memory.

posts.title: Description of a Crying Face
posts.author: Peter White
content: Hills and valleys scar the land,
While summer droughts yield to streams of blood.
Muted thunder seeks to hold our hand,
But clouds roll on, and conceal our sin.
The mind was clear, but now is flooded,
Yet Fall will come, and storms will pass.

posts.title: Longing
posts.author: Peter White
content: I often wish that I will live;
A life that's long but also kind.
But on this hill, or in our hallway,
I feel time change; it stays behind.
My mind expands, but then contracts,
I've stood here now, for far too long.
I missed that future which I never had,
I lost my past in which I did no wrong.
I often wish to become old,
But a life that's long, can become cold.
I mourn my loves before they're gone,
And pray for time to move along.
Now down the hill, or past the hall,
all is well, and life is long.
But time is strange, so I march on.

posts.title: Cardinal (sonnet 3)
posts.author: Peter White
content: Serene I stand amidst the flowers, blue and white.
Until its flash takes from me, all which must be right.
No blood is shed for poets' sake, but hours pass
And feelings fall. The Cardinal now retreats again.
There is a future, where rose buds will bloom at dawn.
Where gunshots one day cease, so fields may fear the fawn.
Mistakes are left inside the past, to lie and rot;
Where I walk free from glen to glen, where he does not.
Serene I'll stand amidst those flowers, blue and white
and wait and pray The Cardinal's Curse stays out of sight.

posts.title: Life According to You
posts.author: Peter White
content: Who are you this time?
The leaf makes its path, and so
you must too. What now?

posts.title: Detritus
posts.author: Peter White
content: Don't give up on it yet.
Every thing and every body;
Though not immediately known,
Retains its one true purpose.
If we stop existing
Then we stop improving.
Unity through decay
Strengthens out bonds in life.

posts.title: Sin
posts.author: Peter White
content: Iron sharpens iron, stone too with stone.
To live on Earth forever, and ever now we must atone.

posts.title: Heron
posts.author: Peter White
content: Things must change, except for my Heron.
On far away shores, it is her I put my faith in.
From the time I was young I envied the sky
for your wings then caressed it, and they will till I die.

posts.title: Divine-ness
posts.author: Peter White
content: To love, and lose, and still be kind;
A feat I keep within my mind.
I fly and fail, such is my curse;
tomorrows will come, until my hearse
To live, and love, to learn true kindness!
This is a testament to His Highness.
Creation loves, and sustains our life.
The answer is there, inside our strife.

posts.title: For Gunner
posts.author: Peter White
content: Lumps and
Death.
Leaps and
Faith.
Love and
You.
Loss for
Me.
Low now,
But not forever, someday soon
I'll remember in tints of rose.

posts.title: The Shepherds Goodbye
posts.author: Peter White
content: But all the love and Worlds remain,
It's gifts that die and minds that change.
Pleasures now ought move us still,
This love of ours rots on the sill.
Spring will end, and then the harvest
So too rocks roll into a far mist.
The gown I've sewn, new shoes and kirtle,
The seeds I've grown to boughs of myrtle.
The scent of posies have been forgotten
You say these pleasures will soon be rotten,
The flowers will fade to wanton fields,
Now here I claim that love won't yield.
Had joys no date, nor age no need
Then still I'd wait, for signs to heed.
I hope for you that pleasures spawn
And move your mind past curtains drawn.

posts.title: Liriope and Laternflys
posts.author: Peter White
content: My thoughts of love and all the light that's shown.
Which is no more, but songs that sing for dusk.
And dusk now gives to black of night. Far blown,
the wind still paints my love as but a husk.
Since many years, and time now can guide me,
Was that love not but sculpture gone to rust?
I played the jury but had no folly;
I killed, and cried for those who stole my trust.

posts.title: Soot to Soil
posts.author: Peter White
content: What's here now is soot
With still burning embers.
Before now were flames,
But no screams and no pain.
Just lookers on,
And the tears that they brought.
Before then was smiles,
And again will there be.
For soot goes to soil,
And the soil to trees.

posts.title: Platanus occidentalis
posts.author: Peter White
content: Always have they been, and will they be, beauty and peace.
Too populous yet individual for any man alone
To see, and know; but still I have pleasure
To think of knowing thee.
Crowned in fall with leaves of gold, You gleam
With grace as your branches fold.
In Spring your hollows bid farewell,
To bears and fawns who within you dwelled. In Summer,
One beholds your might, above the forest
With skin so white. Winter comes
And still you hold dominion, no sight is kinder
To any true Virginian.
A crooked and hollow trunk tells me you remember.
Chestnuts gone, the Ash will follow,
You once housed the Swifts and Swallows.
I see your branches,
Always reaching,
You must still miss them,
And all their teachings.
I feel your pain, great Sycamore, I miss them too--
But it is you that I adore.

posts.title: What's Underneath the Manhole Covers
posts.author: Peter White
content: The rats live forever
Beneath the manhole covers.
In this world there is no man,
No one to catch the plague,
Or eat the pizza first.
Beneath the manhole covers,
The rats live forever and they love to live.
Their kings rule with love
And there is always enough.
There is a world beneath our feet
And as we walk from work to sleep
The rats relax then eat their fill.

posts.title: A View of the Past
posts.author: Peter White
content: I've sat with the song,
RIGHTALIGN
yet I can't seem to listen.
There's a crack in the leaves,
RIGHTALIGN
and the cars and their cries.
The sparrow calls out,
RIGHTALIGN
and her wings send a spell.
I know that they speak but I never
RIGHTALIGN
know if they're speaking to me.
Until one day when
RIGHTALIGN
the wind turns around.
I'm in a new place,
RIGHTALIGN
I feel pleased in this park.
I look back and listen,
RIGHTALIGN
the same song but no lies.
No green leaves cracks,
RIGHTALIGN
and no more do cars cry.
I've tried to ask why,
RIGHTALIGN
but time tells no tales.
I look back again to still the same things,
RIGHTALIGN
and only then do I think, that it's me who has changed.

posts.title: The Virtues
posts.author: Peter White
content: Why should art cry?
And artists despair?
I hear laughter on the breeze
And an ease in the air.

posts.title: Egress
posts.author: Peter White
content: It struck me that all I had to do was turn back. And when I turn, I blink and wet my eyes. The beach is clear, the sun is a furnace. The day is fine but in my hand I hold a gun and fire. The man falls down and I turn again, and still the beach looks quite the same.

It struck me then that instead I could have walked away, thought no more about it. The glints of sun that blinded me, I should have thanked them for hiding her. I walked away, this time through the woods. I blink again but not for eyes that were dry. This time no blood was shed, and I never returned again. In moments since the sun blinds me still; the place we met, the trip we took, those dark old woods. I never could go back, but in my mind it's quite the same.

It struck me then, there may be something more. I’ve walked along inside a seashell whose spirals guided me. It’s tried to show me, but nothing’s changed. It was in that dungeon I locked myself, left no trail, and fell completely. It’s time now I go on my own. I’ll blink until the woods are gone. Until there’s nothing that brings reminding of anything that’s not my own.

posts.title: The Flute Spell
posts.author: Peter White
content: Hard meat don't get eat.
It sits and rots and eats itself.
It stays itself; since no one wants it.
Then bit by bit its grit will split.
It stayed the same, but failed to help;
So it knew no one, and not itself.

posts.title: My Muse
posts.author: Peter White
content: My words come from love
And the good times I've had.
From the time's that I've struggled
But after they've passed.
For dark needs the light,
Not the other way round.

posts.title: What I Saw Out My Window
posts.author: Peter White
content: Crows brought in the night,
The black concealed friends like foes,
And so kings cowered.

posts.title: Old Growth Cemetery
posts.author: Peter White
content: Heavy hang the boughs and branches
On dew dropped mornings when doves still lie.
The forest floor seems dank and rancid
With ghouls and ghosts from times passed
Ferns and orchids can wilt no more;
The ash, the chestnut, and sycamore;
When steam still ruled, their reigns cut short,
Now moss oozes in newborn woods until returns the royal court.

posts.title: Forgetfulness
posts.author: Peter White
content: Beyond the flame; outside the window.
Here in the street, my neighbors weep.
Still in the kitchen; there sits my pencil,
and songs and stories; I'll never speak.
Inside the flames; there is a pureness
And from that pureness; there comes a blankness.
Years will pass; new homes will stand
And then we'll know; that nothing then was ever written.
No pencil laid upon no paper,
No oven burned for far too long,
No food caught flame,
And no one to blame,
No memories of what then was lost.
Beyond the flame; and through the window
I see mistakes that turn to smoke.
I see the pen, I see the paper,
I see in each, my new beginnings.
No songs were sung, nor poems spoken.
Those parts of me are left behind,
Except for now within these verses
Where I confess my one true crime.

posts.title: Jenna’s Coat
posts.author: Peter White
content: Light pours in around the front door;
In golden paths, hardwood becomes worn.
She lies content on Sunday Mornings,
Amber tinted fur upon her, adorning.

posts.title: My Own Perspective
posts.author: Peter White
content: Above I see a weary ship,
It’s traveled far in empty seas,
With battered sails and muted colors
And leagues to go before it moors.
Against a canvas, blinding blue
I share this view with no one else
But at a distance I have to wonder,
Are you on high, searching too for me?

posts.title: Its Absence is a Friend
posts.author: Peter White
content: He walks along a shore
And the ocean is its absence,
Which his boots must ignore
If his journey will continue.
Or instead, he'll walk the boardwalk.
From here the ocean's shrinking
And the ocean is its absence
So its shrinking feels like healing.
Now his life continues like before,
But through the tap the ocean lingers
And in the bath its weight is crushing
And on the shore it felt quite soothing.
So he returned to walk some more
And lift his boots a little higher
And stop to soak it in.
For the ocean is its absence,
So now the ocean is a friend.

posts.title: I Have
posts.author: Peter White
content: And I say to myself: Here is the road that is mine. I have walked its length, in rain I have waded, in snow I have turned and seen only my own prints. I have left, I have returned, but in the Spring when life goes forward, there is still a path nestled in the coneflowers and goldenrod. I have traveled far, lived lives without this road, and gifted it to those I have trusted, but in the woods or on any street, in dark of night or blinding morning clarity I count my steps and see no distance gained. I have learned that I know very little. I have learned that what cannot be left behind by leaving can not be given away, and must be returned to, if not now, a little ways down the road.

posts.title: Pride
posts.author: Peter White
content: There came a time I knew
And took pride in knowing.
Then I learned
And now am content to listen.

posts.title: The Cycle of Soil
posts.author: Peter White
content: All things turn to dust,
But before that they are the soil
And we will be too.
Before then, I will know this green world
And what can be my place.
I will be the soil
and help those in the dust.

posts.title: Ownership
posts.author: Peter White
content: There were years I did not visit,
But grass still grew, and memories,
Like objects, and people, still needed cleaning.
So when I returned, I began
by laying still in the flowers and the past.

posts.title: A Poem For Roger
posts.author: Peter White
content: In the dead and dark
Within damp dens,
I sit and toil toward
your tempting tastes.
Then you slip to sleep
So I may sneak in silence;
revealed from your cupboard, curly
Or from your covers, cautiously.
When you wake with peaceful patience
Laid upon you are my paltry poems.
Cupboard covers readily returned;
Ethereal elves still remaining recluse.

posts.title: Another Chance
posts.author: Peter White
content: The blindfold has fallen
And disappears in the lake.
Lost as tears in the rain,
Or a moth in the flame.
The water is mud;
Who, with malice, slows my pace.
But nothing changes
Without feeling strange
So I stop, in its grasp
And find within me, new space.
I think, it was in love I was found
And now, again, am I bound.

posts.title: Mud
posts.author: Peter White
content: I.
In summer heat
The year’s growth turns dark
And when the tree has fallen
We count it’s life in rings.
II.
If I stay, I’m in the moment
But I don’t plan to leave
And so it is not yet remembered.
III.
I’ll try
All over again
To try
All over again.
But November is nearly past
And I’m ankle deep in the mud.
It’s easier now than one year ago
But there is risk in belonging
And in letting this pass by.
So, I’ll try
All over again
To try
All over again.

posts.title: Pandas at the National Zoo and My Baby Cousin
posts.author: Peter White
content: On the savanna
Between the lions and emus
We stop for lunch and
Begin to grieve the pandas.
"They’re coming back, you know."
RIGHTALIGN
"Yeah, thank God we avoided world war 3."
And Leo stares through us
Towards his courageous namesake.
Today he is older,
I suppose I am too,
But as he smiles, and tries again
To walk like a grown up
I feel excited.
"Can we bring Leo back when the pandas return?" I ask his mother.

posts.title: Thanksgiving Prayer, 2023
posts.author: Peter White
content: There was a time that we, like children,
Assumed a bond prior to its presence,
But now prefer that which is private
Like the timid association of cars
Who follow but never touch their neighbors,
Or two ships passing in the night.
Like dogs on sidewalks pushing against their harnesses,
Trying hard to meet, to succeed at all despite,
Or subway rails that never cross.
I've felt the warmth for those I love,
And I am trying hard to feel it always,
But somedays the flame still cools
And leaves us rigid as the coldness of skyscrapers
Dodging glances across 34th street.
On Thanksgiving day the warmth surrounds
And I remember everyone. I let it warm me to the core.
And try to say to those around me:
If we are ships on Winter nights,
I'll stand outside, and hold my candle.
If we are trains on different lines,
I'll hold my doors, as long as I can handle.
My prayer is that I'll have that strength.
My prayer is that I'll feel the warmth.
At the very least, I'll meet your eyes,
And hear about your day.
At the very least I'll make a seat at my own table,
And I'll be happy when you arrive.

posts.title: Waiting
posts.author: Peter White
content: Winter comes to demand we rest,
So wait for warmth beside the fire

posts.title: Winter
posts.author: Peter White
content: CENTERALIGN
The air stings our lungs
CENTERALIGN
The sun rests too; on long nights
CENTERALIGN
I thank Spring for blooms.

posts.title: The Potomac
posts.author: Peter White
content: The river has run its course
And in my life has become an hour glass
Whose sand will fall, at least a few weeks more
Until I return to measure myself, and how the time has passed.

posts.title: Old Long Since
posts.author: Peter White
content: Another gift to buy,
One more glass on New Year’s Eve,
And still more years on down the line.
I think I’ll give it one more go,
This time, now, for auld lang syne.

posts.title: The burden
posts.author: Peter White
content: I have seen the burden laid by God
That all has beauty in its time.
But to man He gifted memory,
And now we mourn those beauties passed.
So too was man gifted hope,
To dream of futures that never reign.

posts.title: Next Month Again
posts.author: Peter White
content: I never told you
I was saying something new.
It’s been a month
And one full moon
But on these pages
And to your mind
I’m trying hard
To say one thing True.

posts.title: Until Next Year
posts.author: Peter White
content: Let the hour hand fall back,
Let the sun take its rest.
I will sit inside
Bathing in soft warm lights,
Hoping November lasts forever.
And when the calendar turns again,
I'll continue on, into December,
Longer in the tooth,
But no worse for ware.
The days continue passing
But it was then, in November,
That I found who I am.

posts.title: A Conversation with Calypso
posts.author: Peter White
content: "Is it you who makes me stay?
Who controls the waves?
The swaying stalks?
The deadly bays?"
RIGHTALIGN
"And if it were?"
A voice replied,
RIGHTALIGN
"Would you swim ashore?
RIGHTALIGN
Instead face the sky?"
I hold my ground
But tread in the water.
"Cold now, the currents grow,
The sun has set, your shadows totter."
There is no bottom
To this the blackest lake.
And her voice surrounds,
RIGHTALIGN
"Then leave, unless there is more to take."
"But where to go?
If the past has died?"
RIGHTALIGN
"Still on down the stream
RIGHTALIGN
To journeys onward," she softly cries.
I see shadows lean further in
Now serpents cinch, and I suffocate.
Still my voice sounds out, no trace of pain,
"I'll go- just not now. Please, a moment longer."

posts.title: Less Traveled By
posts.author: Peter White
content: Two roads there were
In those woods once yellowed
By summer rains, and many fellows
Who tread the paths,
That are now no where.
Once they wore about the same
Then many moons, and people changed.
Grass and ivy took their time, and rearranged;
By dawn and dusk, never aided by flame,
But still they showed no sign of strain.
More moons passed still,
Somewhere man's regrets now faded,
The yellowed wood, now long degraded,
Held no bird song, no sparrow's trill.
No steps remembered or choices felt,
No beast now knows us, who once walked this hill.

posts.title: A Poem in the Oldest Woods
posts.author: Peter White
content: CENTERALIGN
So
CENTERALIGN
Your
CENTERALIGN
Growth
CENTERALIGN
Is scorched.
CENTERALIGN
By days
CENTERALIGN
Of drought and
CENTERALIGN
Inches gained back in Spring.
CENTERALIGN
Your age is
CENTERALIGN
Marked by how you've changed.
CENTERALIGN
In rings of growth and bark now singed.
CENTERALIGN
The past remains
CENTERALIGN
Though only         where it was.
CENTERALIGN
And one day           roots will rot
CENTERALIGN
Or storms will blow        to prune old limbs.
CENTERALIGN
Another year of growth, and days now gone will wither,
CENTERALIGN
Dry up,
CENTERALIGN
Burn up,
CENTERALIGN
And die.

posts.title: No One
posts.author: Peter White
content: Bald head and bleeding beak,
And arms that block the sun,
And legs like stilts above the dear—
No, it was a fox, but is now no one.
Through throbbing pulses from the throne
One life leaves and I go on.
The rail clicks once, and now they’re gone.
The vulture, and the fox, and their image in my mind.

posts.title: The First Light and Long Since
posts.author: Peter White
content: Wake now.
Rise gently,
And aim to shake the soul.
Shake until dust falls,
Until you always were awake.

posts.title: Mourning for Light
posts.author: Peter White
content: Wind bites down and clamps its maw,
And in its wake the meadow calms.
Black as souls that no love has known,
The sky shows fawns that are not there,
And I hear songs from winter birds.
Cold iron lays limp in my lantern,
And freezes the world where it lays.
One day—and it will have been soon—
The sun will come, and I will mourn
At greater intervals, and pray to Him
In days between.

posts.title: The River to Pray
posts.author: Peter White
content: Clouds above now reflected in you,
In waters which flow but stay so serene,
And carry the dirt from me far away.
Still through the winter, and curtains drawn
The low lying sun burns on my arm,
And shows skin unclean, and bruises unhealed.
Back on your shores the sun now sits higher,
And your currents still reign, under surface so placid.
I’ll scrub in your waters, and I swear I’ll see God;
But the winter still comes and your ways give me pause.
I’ll open the curtains and let the light in
Though its blinding in the morning, So next spring I’ll stay in.

posts.title: The Sea of Tranquility
posts.author: Peter White
content: It’s in still waters I never can sleep,
As your light tries to guide, against the clouds as they leap.
I still steer the ship to a dock that’s not home,
Where we’ve been before but no maps have shown.
Soon the moon sets, another port disappears
But your light still remains to combat my fears
Of the jewel in the sky and the treasure she hides,
And the love of adventure, and a new chance to try.

posts.title: Sun & Moon Sonnet
posts.author: Peter White
content: It was inside the sun that love was found
And in her breast time will tick till all is gone.
Then each night the sun upon the moon rebounds
And so the clock turns back until the dawn.
As days break, the moon remembers its light
And declares that it was in love she was created
And in love she hopes to die.

posts.title: Worth the Night
posts.author: Peter White
content: After first light,
And in that warm motel,
When the first day became the first night.
After that
Began the rest
And so the end arrives.

posts.title: Tied in a Not
posts.author: Peter White
content: In the morning light floods
Through the closed curtains.
Beneath the sheets two will fall
Back to different lives and loves.
Left behind: what could’ve been,
And thank God was not, what was
Prevented and tossed out.
Taken with the morning garbage,
The chance for life and
Today’s ways of waiting for better times.
A blessing and our curse,
The ability to forget
Mistakes, and ignore
What could have been.

posts.title: The Sphinx
posts.author: Peter White
content: I.
He sees
She knows
And so wants to.
He brings
Her gifts
And asks politely
For grace
As mercy
And then he waits.
II.
No answer comes
From sullen eyes.
I see myself
Inside her mirror.
Tinted and obscured.
The sun then sets,
And our eyes close.
Through cold sands I
Turn and muster
The strength I need
To ask again.

posts.title: The Shenandoah
posts.author: Peter White
content: I long to know the Shenandoah
Or some other currents
By another name.
I long to know the Shenandoah
Or at least hear of his power.
The stories of peace he kept,
And the wars that came before.
The stories of his daughter’s beauty,
Which haunts the seas that bear no name.
Or of the tides he learned to tame,
And the beasts that knew his fame.
I long to know, and so adore
A place that binds me to its story.
To know the land and see it change
From abstract art and tales of yore
To kids that know, and still want more
But never from their Shenandoah.

posts.title: Help!
posts.author: Peter White
content: We are stuck
In a tree
And want to be
Free!
Please come and see
Whoever you may be.
Hear our plea!
What?
That is my ladder.
What?
Yes.
I am a fireman.
What? (I’m sorry, you’ll have to excuse my hearing—
I’m quite high off the ground.)
What?
No.
That is not my cat.

posts.title: Elixir of Life
posts.author: Peter White
content: Eye of newt
Tongue of toad
A drop of blood
And touch of lime.
It bubbles and smokes,
And then fills my throat
But it needs something else.
Leave in the liver to liven it up.
Another sip and now we wait…
Though nothing changes, we’ll leave it at that
I’ve tried my best, and must now take a nap.
Tomorrow again I’ll seek out the answer, But first I must harvest the ear of the cat.

posts.title: Sowing What You Reap
posts.author: Peter White
content: In harvest season there is a feast.
Between the neighbors, sons and daughters,
All eat their fill, then go to sleep.
Each year more come, and are invited
To reap the spring’s sowing before the winter
And the coming darkness.
But before the feast has come and gone,
The finest crops must be collected
And their seed allowed to continue on.
In harvest season there is a feast
To fill the air with love and life,
To thank the coming of another dawn.
But more than that, to thank the farmers
Who planted food they’d never eat,
Who planned for shade they’d never see,
Who’ve made our winters a little warmer.

posts.title: Brain Soup
posts.author: Peter White
content: My head is full.
Full of brain soup,
And the brain is nearly ripe,
Nearly wrinkled just enough.
Inside each crevice seeps in the broth
And when i twirl my spoon
My mouth begins to water–
Then my arms don’t work…
Huh– I guess I’ll lift the spoon from my skull
And ignore the side which now droops.
But still I cannot wait another night
To see a brain that’s wrinkled just enough.

posts.title: Egress
posts.author: Peter White
content: The beach is clear, the sun is a furnace.
The day is fine but far too bright and a man
Stands facing me. Even then I knew
I should've turned back, yet in my head there
Was a gun and so I fired. The man fell,
And the flames did not relent, so I blink
And wet my eyes.
Even then, as he stood before me, I knew
I could've walked away toward the shade
And thought no more of it. The glints of sun,
I thank them now as I walk from beaches and
Through the woods. I blink again, beneath
The canopies which shield me from that day.
I hide where no blood is shed, and I never  go
Back. The place we met, the paths we took
Towards that sea. I never could go back but
In my mind its quite the same.
On mountain tops. And Sunny days it still
Pokes through, no matter how quick I turn my head.
Through these windows, the man lays still and
Flaming tendrils steal my vision. I have walked
long towards a day I could forget, but
each path only leads back. I blink to clear
The visions and so my shame. But nothing changes.
Even then, I think I knew this day would come.
When I'd turn back to greet the sun. To see the shadows,
And no longer run. In my mind, that day is the same,
But since the beach it all must change.

posts.title: Harmony
posts.author: Peter White
content: "This is how it ends."
I disagree with strength I cannot muster.
You shake and cannot walk
But I can’t bare to look
For a second,
An eon of moments,
Nor just this instant.
Still you are all that I can see.

posts.title: The Diving Board
posts.author: Peter White
content: Before the board may hold my weight,
Before it crashes down toward the water
And hurls me to the sky, I am pulled
To its edge--
Pulled by the chatter and excitement
That swaddles memories of the Summer;
Pulled by the wait, and the tension in
My chest from waiting some more;
Pulled by fear I haven’t felt since.
That I’ll soar high and land on my back;
That someone will see my awkward descent;
That it hasn’t been 30 minutes
But we’d be leaving soon; that something
Could happen I’d never thought of since.
Behind me and on the pool deck:
Strangers—mostly, that girl
That I loved, and the boy
From school, and the one
I met today, and haven’t seen since.
Their faces seem warped
From the heat of that July day;
From the lens of remembering.
Warped like the board
Who dipped slightly beneath me;
Whose fibers groaned quietly
From the memory of summers
Past, and the thought of even one more august.
Beneath my weight and the board
Stood a brilliant blue mosaic
Warped, too, by ripples and
Dancing sunbeams.
Geometry that, today,
Nestles me in the fur of the past.
A past where I lived, but now
Only visit; where I ran and laughed
And loved, but now only visit;
A past where, when I visit,
I see only the pool—the art
That was beneath it.

posts.title: Cleaning the Hallway
posts.author: Peter White
content: What once could take days
Now takes far less;
There were ghosts in the hall
Who I’ve put to rest.
A whole forest sprouting
Or a mountain top’s view;
Now just a nap
Or a morning’s fresh dew.
The sheets are now folded
Not covering faces;
Sometimes the laundry alone
Is what makes safe spaces.

posts.title: The Same Path, Once More
posts.author: Peter White
content: This will be the last time
We walk this path together –
We thought, defeated.
But that was then, and here we are
Your paws submerged in the dead brown pond.
Again you lived to swim
And again you walked home
Through the woods, down the lane, still toward another winter.
This will be the last time
I think, thankful
For how you’ve proved us wrong before.
But that was then, and now is different.
Your bowl is never emptied now,
You need help off the ground now,
And death is not a stranger but
Now a mass in your brain.
This—inevitable
This will be the last time,
And it will have been enough.

posts.title: Annual Desires
posts.author: Peter White
content: First I want
To live simply,
Then to save the world.
Next I want
To write
And so I write.
First comes Spring,
And then Summer.
Next is Fall
And then the Winter.

posts.title: Return
posts.author: Peter White
content: A loon toward his lake—
Bloodshot eyes and new scars
To show his lover.
The time alone
Spent in bed
After late nights.
Homely, welcoming curves—
On familiar roads
That started far away.
True voyage is return.
As the hound knows—
Briefly breaking out
With dreams of fowl
Trapped in his maw.
He bounds through prairie
And ducks from branches
Then slows the heart
And heads back home.
With slobbered memories
Of life unbound, with
A tail that says
He’s glad he’s found.

posts.title: Posture of a Mother
posts.author: Peter White
content: Always leaning under the weight
Of children beared on broad hips.
A rear view mirror skewed too far
So the back seat is always in view.
Her home kept just so-
So, when they grow up and come back,
INDENT
They still fit.
So, there is space on the couch for all,
INDENT
Even if she has to squeeze between dogs.
So any guests that enter are reminded
INDENT
Of their own; so they are welcomed in
INDENT
To a mother's- in to their home.

posts.title: Proclamation or Promise
posts.author: Peter White
content: I wouldn't say it if I didn't mean it
Or I would and wish I hadn't
And wish you could hear my thoughts-
Bathe in my sincerity.
I would not say it
If I could help it
If today were next year
So I could be who I am
Not now.

posts.title: The Stand
posts.author: Peter White
content: Love grows old
INDENT
And walks away.
The home's creaking boards
Forget my name
As the neighbors drain the beaver pond.
The grief lasts forever.

posts.title: Route 28 South
posts.author: Peter White
content: Where is the regret?
Not in his wicked smile
But please be behind it,
Since it is also held in
Clasped fingers losing blood flow
Tightening and turning white.
The deer struck and crumpled now
But not one car has slowed down.
Where is the regret
In his rear view mirror?
Please be hiding your pain.
INDENT
Please.
INDENT
Please,
INDENT
INDENT
have pity for a life's ending
INDENT
INDENT
in a place that was not made for it.
INDENT
INDENT
Let me loose my fingers' pleading.
INDENT
INDENT
And feel- with me- the Earth
INDENT
INDENT
growing heavy behind diaphragms,
INDENT
INDENT
mine, yours,
INDENT
INDENT
INDENT
and impossibly peaceful Death's.

posts.title: Dawn
posts.author: Peter White
content: The sun still rises
And through the dark
Its beam still slices.
Summers come and go
But in the Winter
It still melts the snow.
When the night gives in to hate
It’s light that says, "love is stronger."
And when the sun is more than late,
Still, the dawn won’t be much longer.

posts.title: Thirst
posts.author: Peter White
content: I drank, on my hands and knees
Not with depth, but with greed.
As if I had never drank
As if the world were under a mile of sand
And suddenly the sky broke.
When the rain finally ceased
My lips were mud without the sea,
Cracked and bloody-- I was drunk
With new sensation. Thirst worse than before--
Before a brush with sustaining wonder.

posts.title: Hunger
posts.author: Peter White
content: Translucent, pale green complexion
The kind that belongs only to a stranger
Whose spine creates serration,
Whose ribs are smothered
Collapsing under tensioned skin
And the weight of hunger.
It finds itself among a flock, with no protection,
of soft, plump clouds gently grazing.
In an instant blood is flowing like salvation:
A divine gluttony, impossible but filling
Until it is full and its heart
Can stop beating,
From one last act- then depravation.

posts.title: Uni Kuru Toga
posts.author: Peter White
content: Luster lacking, after lasting labor,
Sitting still, scratched, and stained
With oils and dead skin,
And an eraser lost--
I'm not sure when.
Banal, bent bits, and broken
Plastic. Pencils pushed passed expiration,
Or brought along willfully.
When I write, I think of you
And how things are a part of me.

posts.title: The Stand
posts.author: Peter White
content: Sandy soil
Housing funny plants
Ticklish to the touch.
And nothing much around.
Swings that creak
And fly me through the fire
Smoke. A taste of s'mores
And once an oyster.
Soft, soft bread, and couches
And a rocking chair
In a room we all would pack in.
An attempt to let it all live on.
Acceptance that its gone.
The Stand
A place of vast- and close-ness
A chance for grace from egress.

posts.title: Fall Light
posts.author: Peter White
content: Pale but bright
Empty space
Early sun, sets
To golden rays.
From dawn till dusk:
Pervasive, probing,
Asking why with biting winds
And a long night to think
Of an answer.

posts.title: The Limb
posts.author: Peter White
content: Rotten, falling off in bits,
Blown away by a bomb,
Or carefully, surgically removed.
It makes no difference.
The Limb is gone.
Sometimes when they're all still there,
Sometimes - every time - you drive on one road.
Or think you hear a name on the wind.
The journey is in the return.

posts.title: Perfect Days
posts.author: Peter White
content: The sun rose, second.
Shown softly, in apology
On the window’s sill.
Even my breath is music.

posts.title: Dependable Light
posts.author: Peter White
content: Crawling tendrils lose their strength
As evening nestles in, first in the valleys
Then to my home.
Today, its light: a brother,
Other times, it is a friend.
Sometimes the light canters on-
Even past the numbing clouds-
A messenger, and the first to console.
Sometimes he comes, wise and unassuming
To guide me on paths I cannot see.
So when his grip falls tired across the lawn
I let mine do the same
And trust the day will come again.

posts.title: Worship
posts.author: Peter White
content: Clouds fall quilted
On the first
Evening since clocks turned back
Glowing with that
Light created--
When I close my eyes
And slowly open
Or dust the altar of my pleasure
Created light floods the station
Pours through every window
Sneaks in, as I rest to its end

posts.title: My Rock, My River
posts.author: Peter White
content: Buried Deep
--as long as could matter
You sift and search
--until freed
Turbulent and Tumbling at times
--until water runs clear, and settles again
My rock
--my river
Until river is sea
--until I am not me.

posts.title: Two Ships on the Subway
posts.author: Peter White
content: Inches from good
Steps from different
Turned just by half
To begin anew

posts.title: Pray Without Ceasing
posts.author: Peter White
content: Pray without ceasing
And without any church.
Pray without words
except these: I love you
Without the altar
Or any ancient rules
Pray without ceasing
And don't dare tell God,
Unless They are yours
(so can be called You)
Unless They can change
And you'd say it the same.

posts.title: Wound up here
posts.author: Peter White
content: By a finger
or a thread,
Only trying to add more.

posts.title: Dark Eyed Junco
posts.author: Peter White
content: With love in my Right Hand,
A Soul in the left.
All creation is a friend
And a friend is one
I listen to.
They need not hear
me speak, or know
My life at all.
A friend is one
I listen to
And trust, and love,
And believe is True.

posts.title: Far
posts.author: Peter White
content: I.
Not far enough.
The Spring pf sprung hamstrings failed to flight me flying
But my starting point was far from the ledge.
Toppled turning, toes over tit
Twirling with out
Control-- that made it feel certain--
Like twisting, tilted was the way it was
The Spring resets
As Springs do.
The ledge greeted me quickly,
And stunned me again and again
As ledge meeting noses will do.
Faithful
The Spring continued, unaware.
Or just unwilling.
That is: without will.
II.
But not as far
Or farther, but at least in a new direction
Now for certain
Side stepped, Sunken, Soaring still
The only constant was the Spring.
III.
And far enough
To twist, twirl, top turned toward teh ground
and not!
Not
The ledge
And nothing now to set the Spring against.

posts.title: Comfort Food
posts.author: Peter White
content: Meals that fill the house
as if announcing their arrival
A scent and comfort, potent, ontollogical.
While I wait, I wait;
A poem's first reading
before April may prove its intents
A light that is fleeting
and a sparrow "cheet-cheeting"
crows and mocking birds toss out their calls
and cardinals are bleeting
Still the sauce simmers
While tasks to be done are resigned
To tomorrow, and sent with a sigh
Still the sauce simmers
And the air still feels lighter
While this comfort compresses
And still the sauce simmers

posts.title: Healing
posts.author: Peter White
content: I know no knots
that tether kindly.
Soft yet firm
Secure and supple.
I hold you tight
and look away.
But on return
my grip's a noose.
Focus then, to tie it different.
Focused effort, is one day habit.

posts.title: Her
posts.author: Peter White
content: If I were [Joaquin Phoenix]
I'd fall for Her too
Or, today, not fall but leap
Not a leap of passionate certainty
Destined at death to vacillate to apathy
Leap of faith
In me,
and my faculties
Trust in my strength
And the ability of my legs to fling me far
And far enough to not clip the edge.

posts.title: Untitled
posts.author: Peter White
content: You don't have to
Turn that stone.
Things happen
I wish had not.
I wish I had not.
The stone is still there
It'll bleed when you make it.

posts.title: To Find the Path
posts.author: Peter White
content: Trusting lively premonitions
Neglecting past admissions,
Acceptance of omissions
When it speaks
It speaks to me
In moments peaking
From the future,
As guidance,
If I'll listen

posts.title: Bel Air Diner
posts.author: Peter White
content: Clasped hands
Holding an old friendship
A photo  captured,
Commemorated the child's ecstasy
One more cup
Before the next
Or first order a milkshake
with breakfast,
And a server
That fits herself

posts.title: Bones
posts.author: Peter White
content: Flowing out
And arranged--
Like the order of drops
On a pane,
Or leaves piled in the fall--
As if there were
No other option.
A poem can feel
Like a fist.

posts.title: The Garden of Eden
posts.author: Peter White
content: I won't walk
A single step
Unless you journey, too.
I won't eat
Even one seed
Unless the planting is provisioned.
All flourishing is mutual;
And I wouldn't think to,
Without you.

posts.title: Stills
posts.author: Peter White
content: Sun bleached,
Whitening, contrast starkening
Before fading into sameness
An expression that is no longer mine,
But a feeling I am still within
Printed
Obtained, and so
Vulnerable to loss;
Obtained and so indebted
To protection
To the labor that brings to being;
Obtained and so committed
To memory
And open to ache--
Take the photo, still.

posts.title: November Affirmations
posts.author: Peter White
content: To love what is mine
Without claiming stake
To love what I am of
And that I may be bound--
Tethered to inconvenience
That I may serve toward
Such tasks without hesitation
That I may do so,
Especially when it is not easy
That I may do so,
And renew this vow in a year:
To love what is mine
Without claiming stake
To love what I am of
And that I may be bound.

posts.title: Communing
posts.author: Peter White
content: Let's go for a walk
One with words and open spaces.
I wanted more from our talk-
So I ask and hear
The outdoor's phrases

posts.title: Paneer
posts.author: Peter White
content: Simply sustaining
Unexpected and complete
So mundane as to seem divine
I learn every year
How good this can be
Simple and sustaining
Without expectations.
Complete.
I learn every year.

posts.title: Grateful
posts.author: Peter White
content: the sun may rise too
Soon while I still rest
Or set behind a curtain of clouds.
My legs may cease their carrying
While my arms lose dexterity
No one will ever be there
Through it all
But the Earth still spins,
My heart still beats
And they are here now.

posts.title: Love as Witness
posts.author: Peter White
content: It is not mine
except to see
except the pull to linger,
In the morning
In the grocery
wondering if you are in need
You are not mine
except to witness,
and think about when work is slow,
and to bound my vision onto beauty
What is mine is this:
The promise to see,
To witness, to renew this
Promise in a year.

posts.title: Novembers' Exit
posts.author: Peter White
content: This could be what it looks like;
Eyes settled,
Content to soften focus
Toward the window.
To welcome nights
And wait eagerly for dawn.
It might just look like
The days when November
Bleeds in to December.
When the year ends,
The next now in sight.

posts.title: When This is The Start
posts.author: Peter White
content: I begin to know The End.
When this is how it starts--
The front porch sun,
on everyday wrinkling skin;
The swing we will build
(have built),
in the old oak;
The gray you've started
growing, long after mine
-- All comes into focus
And the light from
Prophetic visions bends
(exactly like a memory).
When this is The Start,
All my thoughts bend
toward a smile;
And all my heart wants that ending;
Then the beating calms
For knowledge It is Ours.

posts.title: Neighborly
posts.author: Peter White
content: I start to feel--
as the bus kneels
and the Dog's Bark quiets,
remembering my routine
--like there is space.
For me, or (I pray to remember)
There is space for another,
Stood on the curb.
With every reason to see.
There is space.
For one more, on that never full bus
In hard times,
Food is kept in the belly of a brother.

posts.title: Haircuts
posts.author: Peter White
content: Make it worth going to church,
To write about that act
Of periodic observance
Or better said, continued viewing.
Where I'm at now is this:
I when you'll cut your hair
And I I wait with meaning forming.
My best guess is that's the same.

posts.title: THE MAW THAT KNOWS NOT
posts.author: Peter White
content: A stone rolls between molars
Tripping and betraying words
That are dented and bent
They sound sharp, to be avoided,
And leave blood smeared on the tongue,
Drawn from those nearby
The stone rolls without tasting;
Singed ever darker, and red.
Then, round.
